title: Hybrid evidence packaging: RBAC, audit logs, and residency blueprint
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary:

This blueprint describes a unified approach to packaging and preserving compliance evidence for hybrid deployments (hosted + private/VPC). It ties RBAC attestations, structured audit logs, and data-residency metadata into a reproducible evidence bundle suitable for regulatory audits, incident response, and internal controls reviews. The goal is to reduce time-to-evidence, improve tamper-resistance, and ensure residency controls are transparent across deployment modes.

Scope:

- Applies to: Redwood-hosted API, Dedicated clusters, Private/VPC deployments, and on-prem agent collectors.
- Evidence types: RBAC entitlement snapshots, access attestation logs, structured audit events (API/authz), system and application logs required for forensics, data-residency manifests and custody chain.
- Excludes: Third-party vendor logs (see third-party evidence integration section).

Owners and stakeholders:

- Primary owner: Security (evidence-orchestration squad)
- Stakeholders: Compliance, Legal, SRE, Platform, Customer Success, Product Security
- Evidence custodian (per-case): Service owner listed on each evidence bundle

Goals and acceptance criteria:

1. Evidence bundle generation within 4 hours of request (automated) or <24 hours if manual attestations required.
2. Evidence completeness score >= 95% (per checklist) for standard audit requests.
3. Tamper-evident packaging: signed artifacts with KMS-backed signing keys.
4. Residency flags preserved for all artifacts; bundle indicates regional storage/processing.

Definitions:

- Evidence bundle: a time-bound, signed archive containing machine-readable artifacts and a human-readable index.
- Attestation: a signed statement from an owner/service confirming configuration/role state at a timestamp.
- Custody chain: ordered sequence of transfers or accesses for an artifact (who had access, when).

High-level architecture components:

- authz-service: produces role definitions and entitlement snaps via /v1/entitlements API.
- audit-collector: ingests structured events and forwards to the evidence pipeline (Kafka topic: audit-evidence-ingest).
- evidence-orchestrator: serverless pipeline that collects artifacts, normalizes metadata, signs bundles, and writes to evidence-store (S3 bucket: s3://evidence-packages-prod).
- evidence-store: versioned object store with object-lock enabled; keys encrypted with kms-redwood-evidence.
- residency-registry: service mapping tenant IDs to residency zones and retention policies.

Evidence mapping matrix (table):

| Artifact | Source service | Format | Retention class | Residency flag | Required for audit? |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| RBAC snapshot | authz-service /v1/entitlements | JSON (schema v2) | 7 years (high-sensitivity) | yes | Required |
| Access logs (authn/authz) | audit-collector | JSONL (structured) | 2 years | yes | Required |
| System process logs | node-agent | text/zip | 1 year | depends | Recommended |
| Data custody manifest | residency-registry | YAML | 7 years | yes | Required if cross-border |
| Application trace (sampled) | tracing-proxy | OTLP/JSON | 90 days | no | Optional |

Automated bundle generation (preferred flow):

1. Trigger: Compliance ticket created or automated retention reconciliation job.
2. evidence-orchestrator queries residency-registry for tenant residency metadata.
3. Orchestrator calls authz-service to request entitlement snapshot (snapshot_id).
4. Orchestrator subscribes to audit-evidence-ingest Kafka topic to collect relevant log windows (bounded by start_ts/end_ts).
5. Artifacts are normalized (schema v2) and hashed (SHA256).
6. Signed manifest.json is produced containing artifact metadata, SHA256 hashes, timestamps, and custody chain entries. Manifest is signed with KMS key kms-redwood-evidence using RSASSA-PSS.
7. Bundle (tar.gz) is uploaded to s3://evidence-packages-prod/<tenant>/<bundle-id>.tar.gz with object-lock retention per residency policy.
8. Notification to requestor + Compliance Slack channel, and record stored in compliance-case DB.

Manual collection procedure (when automation cannot access private VPC artifacts):

1. Create compliance ticket with required artifact list and timeframe.
2. If customer-managed collector required, instruct on secure upload: SFTP endpoint + pre-signed temporary object URL with minimum TTL and IP restrictions.
3. Collectors must include a local manifest.yaml with checksums and a signed owner attestation (PGP or provided KMS-signed blob).
4. Once uploaded, evidence-orchestrator verifies checksums and appends uploaded artifacts into the signed bundle.

RBAC attestation checklist (per-bundle):

- [ ] Export of all roles, policies, and group memberships for affected tenant. (authz-service /v1/entitlements?snapshot=true)
- [ ] Snapshot includes role-to-resource mapping, role conditions, and last-changed metadata.
- [ ] Owner attestation present for any emergency privileges (privileged_escalation entries).
- [ ] Evidence of role reviews (last attestation timestamp) from the entitlement-review service.

Audit logging: collection and structure

- Log format: structured JSON schema v1.3 (fields: timestamp, tenant_id, service, principal_id, action, resource, decision, metadata).
- Retention classes are enforced by the audit-collector via routing rules (daily partitions).
- Indexing: All audit logs pushed to secure Elasticsearch (tiered nodes) with read-only snapshots preserved to evidence-store monthly.
- Example query to extract events for bundle window (CLI):

  # Query via audit-query-cli (internal)
  audit-query-cli --tenant T-12345 --start 2028-11-01T00:00:00Z --end 2028-11-30T23:59:59Z --format jsonl > authz-events.jsonl

- Note: for private deployments the audit-collector agent ships an encrypted bundle to the evidence-orchestrator endpoint using mutual TLS.

Data residency & retention mapping (concise table):

| Residency zone | Default log retention | Evidence object-lock duration | Comments |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| NA (us-west-2, us-east-1) | 2 years | 7 years | Standard US residency; legal hold support |
| EU (eu-central-1) | 2 years | 7 years | GDPR considerations; encryption-at-rest with region KMS |
| APAC (ap-southeast-1) | 1 year | 5 years | Varies by country; escalate for cross-border requests |

Secure SDLC gating for evidence capabilities:

- Feature owners must include evidence hooks in the PR: unit tests for artifact schema, integration test that triggers evidence-orchestrator stub, and docs for residency flags.
- Release checklist items (required):
  1. Schema compatibility check (backward/forward).
  2. Keys for signing present in staging KMS.
  3. End-to-end test that generates a sample bundle and uploads to test evidence-store.
  4. Security review sign-off for credential handling.

Incident response tie-ins:

- Preservation order: If an incident is declared, SRE calls the evidence-orchestrator preserve API to immediately snapshot ongoing logs and apply object-lock for the case id.
- Chain-of-custody: Incident responders must log all accesses to the evidence bundle in the incident-case tracker and append custody events to manifest.json.
- For suspected exfiltration, enable high-fidelity collection window and request forensic-level artifacts (full system images) via the forensics-playbook.

Tamper-evidence and signing details:

- All bundles must include a manifest.json with SHA256 hashes for every file and a KMS-backed signature (RSASSA-PSS).
- Verification process: verification-cli verify --bundle <path> --public-key /keys/evidence-proving.pem returns PASS/FAIL and lists any mismatches.

Operational runbook (short):

1. Ticket received -> validate scope and residency -> assign evidence owner (1 business hour).
2. Attempt automated collection -> if success, close within SLA (4 hours).
3. If manual artifacts required, coordinate with customer/SRE -> set manual SLA (24 hours).
4. Run post-package QA (checksum, signature, manifest completeness).
5. Upload to evidence-store and mark case as "packaged".

SLAs and metrics:

- Evidence generation time (automated): P95 <= 4 hours.
- Bundle verification success rate: >= 99.5% within 24 hours of packaging.
- Evidence availability (S3): 99.9% monthly uptime.

Templates and examples (appendix):

- Sample manifest.json (abbreviated):
  {
    "bundle_id": "EB-20290220-9f2a",
    "tenant_id": "T-12345",
    "created_at": "2029-02-20T10:12:00Z",
    "artifacts": [
      { "path": "rbac/snapshot-2028-11-30.json", "sha256": "3a7...", "size": 13421 },
      { "path": "audit/authz-events.jsonl", "sha256": "b5c...", "size": 241234 }
    ],
    "manifest_signature": "base64-sig=="
  }

- Example evidence-orchestrator invocation (CLI):
  evidence-orchestrator create-bundle --tenant T-12345 --start 2028-11-01T00:00:00Z --end 2028-11-30T23:59:59Z --output ./EB-202811-T12345.tar.gz

Third-party integration notes:

- For vendor-managed logs, request a signed export and manifest.yaml from the vendor. The evidence-orchestrator will not accept unsigned artifacts unless a documented attestation is included.
- If legal constraints prevent transfer, preserve a hashed pointer to the vendor archive and include the vendor-signed attestation in the bundle.

Privacy and legal considerations:

- Redact PII from non-forensic artifacts where appropriate. For forensic requests, follow the legal hold workflow and coordinate with Legal before un-redacting.
- All cross-border transfers must be routed through the residency-registry and approved by the Data Protection Officer for the tenant.

Rollout plan and milestones:

- Q1 2029: Pilot with two enterprise customers for hybrid bundles and validate automation latency.
- Q2 2029: Enforce signed manifests on all hosted bundles and integrate verification-cli into release checks.
- Q3 2029: Expand evidence-store region parity for EU and APAC with cross-region replication limited to residency-approved keys.

References and related artifacts:

- authz-service API spec: /internal/specs/authz-service.md
- audit-log schema v1.3: /internal/specs/audit-schema-v1.3.yaml
- Evidence signing standard: /security/standards/evidence-signing-standards-2028.md
- Forensics playbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/forensic-log-preservation-and-legal-hold-playbook-2025.json

Appendix: quick checklist for Compliance reviewers:

- [ ] Bundle contains signed manifest.json
- [ ] RBAC snapshot present and owner-attested
- [ ] Residency manifest included and matches custody entries
- [ ] Hashes verified and verification-cli PASS
- [ ] Object-lock and retention settings applied correctly
